a_records.quote: Let X1 and X2 be two p-dimensional random vectors such that X1 ~ ST_p(xi_1, Omega_1, alpha_1, nu_1) and X2 ~ ST_p(xi_2, Omega_2, alpha_2, nu_2). If nu_1 <= nu_2 then X2 <=c-tw X1.

records.claim: Section 4 application: decade-wise c-tw comparison of ST-fitted maximum temperatures
records.quote: The evolution of extreme episodes along time can be assessed by the estimation of the tail weight parameter nu of the ST model from data for all the decades under consideration. ... It can be observed a decreasing trend along the time, which means that temperatures have evolved towards more extreme summers along time.
records.family: multivariate ST fitted to Iberian Peninsula maximum-temperature data (three climate scenarios: Atlantic, Continental, Mediterranean)
records.compared: decade-wise fitted ST models, decades 1901-1910 through 2001-2010

hypotheses.text: ST model fitted to each decade's summer maxima

conclusion.direction: estimated nu decreases along time, so by Proposition 5 later decades are more tail weighted: X_later >=_{c-tw} X_earlier (equivalently earlier <=c-tw later)

records.numbers: no numeric nu estimates printed in text (only Fig. 3 plot; Mardia kurtosis estimates in Tables 1-3)
records.ambiguity: Empirical application via parameter estimation and Proposition 5; not an analytic example.
